name: The Verge
summary: Tech editorial media. Acid-mint and ultraviolet accents, Manuka display type

colors.name: Jelly Mint
colors.role: The Verge's signature acid-mint accent. Used as CTA button fill, link underlines, active tab borders, and high-attention story-tile backgrounds. Treat it as the visual equivalent of neon safety paint — applied sparingly to the most important element on screen.

colors.name: Verge Ultraviolet
colors.role: The complementary brand hazard. Used for secondary color-block tiles, promotional spans, and the occasional outlined button. Often applied at 0.9 alpha to soften its cathode intensity.

colors.name: Console Mint Border
colors.role: A darker variant of the jelly mint used on card outlines and button borders where pure mint would over-saturate.

colors.name: Deep Link Blue
colors.role: The link *hover* color — the one moment blue appears on the site. It replaces mint/white/black on hover across every link style.

colors.name: Focus Cyan
colors.role: Reserved for button focus rings. Never shown outside a keyboard-focus state.

colors.name: Purple Rule
colors.role: A darker ultraviolet variant used as the vertical border on StoryStream `<li>` items.

colors.name: Canvas Black
colors.role: The default dark surface for the entire homepage. Almost-but-not-quite pure black — has just enough warmth to feel like a printed newsprint negative rather than an OLED void.

colors.name: Surface Slate
colors.role: Secondary card background, used when a story tile doesn't need to be a saturated color block.

colors.name: Image Frame
colors.role: The 1px border that wraps inline imagery.

colors.name: Hazard White
colors.role: Used as story-tile fill, button border, and primary text. When white appears as a large block, it's an editorial decision — a "spotlight" on that tile.

colors.name: Absolute Black
colors.role: Reserved for text on the mint/yellow/white tiles — the only place it appears.

colors.name: Primary Text
colors.role: Headlines and display text on the canvas.

colors.name: Secondary Text
colors.role: Bylines, timestamps, photo credits. The mid-gray that anchors the metadata layer.

colors.name: Muted Text
colors.role: Button text on dark slate buttons. Slightly off-white to reduce screen glare.

colors.name: Inverted Text
colors.role: Used only on accent tiles (mint, yellow, white) to keep contrast legible.

colors.name: Dim Gray
colors.role: Active/pressed button background — the "pressed down" state.

substitutesNote: The 0.80 line-height on Manuka display (107px, 90px, 60px) assumes the **proprietary Manuka face from Klim Type Foundry**, which has aggressively tight vertical metrics designed for athletic stance at large sizes. If you substitute with wide-metric open-source condensed displays like **Anton**, **Oswald**, **Bebas Neue**, or **Archivo Black**, loosen display line-heights by approximately **+0.10 to +0.15** to prevent ascender/descender collisions (e.g., 0.80 → 0.95). PolySans substitutes (Space Grotesk, DM Sans, Hanken Grotesk) work at the token values without adjustment — their metrics are close enough. PolySans Mono substitutes (Space Mono, JetBrains Mono) and FK Roman substitutes (Newsreader, Literata) also work without adjustment.
